newsitem.title: UK: US stocks mixed in quiet dealings in London.
newsitem.headline: US stocks mixed in quiet dealings in London.

text.p: U.S. stocks were mixed in thin trading in London on Wednesday after Tuesday's record-setting rally on Wall Street.
"The market is at key levels where it looks like it wants to break out and go higher, but people are loath to pre-empt that," said one London dealer.

He noted some interest in shares in International Business Machines Corp with the two-for-one stock split in effect. The shares were trading up $1/4 at $89-3/4 on a post-split basis, having soared to a record on Wall Street on Tuesday.
The technology sector led Tuesday's advance, driving the S&P 500 and the Nasdaq Composite indices into uncharted territory, as well as the benchmark Dow average.
But other technology stocks were narrowly mixed in London, with shares in Intel Corp down $1/4 on profit-taking and Digital Equipment Corp up $1/8 on follow through buying, dealers said.
"There's really no strong trend there," said another dealer.
In other trading, shares in Philip Morris Cos Inc eased $1/4 to $44-1/2 in London on growing worries about the first ever class action anti-smoking case set to go to trial in a Florida court.
Shares in AT&T Corp slipped $1/8 to $37-3/8 in London after jumping $1-3/8 in New York on Tuesday amid speculation the telecommunications giant would merge with SBC Communications Inc .
"The (AT&T) stock has died a slow death," the dealer said. "I've hardly had an inquiry on it."
Elsewhere, June S&P 500 index futures were down 0.80 at 850.55 on Globex at 1015 GMT, while June long bond futures were off 2/32 at 108-21/32.
London dealers were looking for a mixed opening on Wall Street, but said the market could be influenced by data on durable goods, due to be published at 1230 GMT.
Orders for durable goods are expected to have risen 2.2 percent in April after a 2.6 percent drop in March. --Debra Sherman, London Newsroom +44 171 542 5106
